title: to_dict returns signing_secret, so the list endpoint hands the secret back on every GET
what_is_wrong: list_webhook_endpoints serialises each endpoint with to_dict, which includes signing_secret, so the HMAC key is readable at any time by anyone with a session token.

title: deliveries endpoint is not scoped to the caller's org
what_is_wrong: the query filters only on WebhookDelivery.endpoint_id taken from the path, so any authenticated user can enumerate delivery rows belonging to another organization's endpoints.

title: no SSRF guard on the registered host
what_is_wrong: the URL is accepted after a scheme/netloc check only, so a customer can register http://127.0.0.1/, http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal DNS name and have the worker POST to it from inside the network.

title: scheme check accepts http:// and any scheme with an http prefix
what_is_wrong: `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` is true for `http`, `httpx` and `httpfoo`, so plaintext and bogus schemes pass validation.

title: limit has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` allows `?limit=100000000`, letting a client pull an unbounded number of delivery rows in one request.

title: event_types is stored without validation against known event types
what_is_wrong: the list from the request body is written straight to the JSONB column, so typos or arbitrary strings are persisted and silently never match any dispatched event.

title: organizations.webhooks_enabled is never consulted
what_is_wrong: the migration adds the per-org feature flag but endpoint creation ignores it, so orgs with the feature off can still register endpoints.

title: url field has no length or format constraint
what_is_wrong: `url: str` accepts a megabyte-long string which is stored in a TEXT column and later logged and used as a request target.

title: endpoint listing has no pagination or limit
what_is_wrong: `.all()` returns every endpoint row for the org, so response size grows without bound.

title: no cap on endpoints per org and no duplicate-URL check
what_is_wrong: nothing stops a client from creating unlimited identical endpoints, each of which multiplies outbound fan-out per event.

title: no route to deactivate, delete, or rotate an endpoint
what_is_wrong: only create and read routes are added, so the `active` flag is unreachable and a leaked signing secret can never be rotated.

title: response body is built from the flushed-but-uncommitted row
what_is_wrong: `to_dict()` is evaluated inside the session scope after `flush()`, so the 201 payload is produced before the transaction commits and a commit failure still yields a serialised endpoint.

title: webhook rows are enqueued in a separate transaction from the event insert
what_is_wrong: the event's `session_scope` has already committed when `enqueue_for_event` opens its own session, so a failure between the two leaves a persisted event with no delivery rows.

title: enqueue failure is swallowed as a warning
what_is_wrong: `except Exception` logs and continues, so a broken enqueue silently drops the webhook for that event while the docs promise at-least-once delivery.

title: hardcoded three-type allowlist contradicts the empty-event_types contract
what_is_wrong: only `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed` and `subscription.updated` reach the webhook path, so an endpoint with empty `event_types` receives nothing for any other event the system emits.

title: webhooks_enabled is not checked before enqueueing
what_is_wrong: the org-level flag added by the migration is never read, so deliveries are created for orgs where webhooks are meant to be off.

title: webhook enqueue runs inline in the caller's request path
what_is_wrong: `await webhook_delivery.enqueue_for_event(...)` performs a synchronous endpoint query and insert before `dispatch` returns, adding fan-out cost to whatever produced the event.

title: an exception from any in-process subscriber prevents the webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: the unguarded `for subscriber ...: await subscriber(envelope)` loop sits before the webhook block, so one failing subscriber cancels webhook delivery for the event.

title: the delivered body is the bare envelope payload with no event id or type
what_is_wrong: only `envelope.payload` is passed through to the delivery row and then POSTed, so receivers cannot deduplicate on `event_id` as the docs instruct because it is not in the body.

title: the signature is computed over different bytes than the request body
what_is_wrong: `sign()` HMACs `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while the request is sent with `client.post(json=...)`, whose serialisation differs in key order and separators, so a receiver hashing the raw body never reproduces the signature.

title: blocking time.sleep inside an async coroutine
what_is_wrong: `time.sleep(delay)` stalls the whole event loop for up to 16 seconds, freezing every other delivery in the gathered batch and the worker's polling.

title: ORM rows are returned after their session is closed
what_is_wrong: the rows are fetched inside `with session_scope()` and returned, so every later attribute read in `deliver` touches a detached instance and raises DetachedInstanceError.

title: endpoint is loaded and then used outside its session
what_is_wrong: `endpoint = session.get(...)` is the only statement in the `with` block, so `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` in `send_once` are read from a detached instance.

title: the lock is a non-atomic get-then-set
what_is_wrong: two workers that both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` will both `set` it and both proceed, so the mutual exclusion the design relies on does not hold.

title: SET and EXPIRE are separate commands
what_is_wrong: if the process dies between them the key has no TTL, and all webhook delivery stops permanently until someone deletes the key by hand.

title: the lock is deleted without an ownership check
what_is_wrong: the `finally` block calls `redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` unconditionally, so a worker whose 60s TTL already expired deletes the lock now held by a different worker.

title: 60s TTL is shorter than a batch's worst-case runtime
what_is_wrong: 100 deliveries with 30s timeouts and 2+4+8+16s sleeps far exceed 60s, so the lock expires mid-batch and a second worker starts processing the same table.

title: claim query has no row locking
what_is_wrong: the SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status update is not conditional, so concurrent workers or instances select the same pending rows and deliver them twice.

title: rows set to in_flight are never returned to pending
what_is_wrong: nothing resets `in_flight` after a crash, cancellation, or unhandled exception, and no reaper exists, so those deliveries are excluded from the pending filter forever.

title: retry state is kept only in a local variable
what_is_wrong: `attempt` is incremented in memory and `attempts`/`next_attempt_at` are written only by `_finish`, so a restart mid-retry loses all attempt history and the row's scheduled time.

title: 4xx responses are retried
what_is_wrong: the loop retries every non-2xx status until MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a permanent 400 or 404 costs five attempts instead of stopping immediately as documented.

title: backoff has no jitter
what_is_wrong: `timedelta(seconds=BASE_DELAY_SECONDS**attempt)` is fully deterministic, so all deliveries failing at the same moment retry in lockstep.

title: naive datetime written into a timezone-aware column
what_is_wrong: `next_attempt_at=datetime.utcnow()` produces a naive value while `_claim_batch` compares against `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, mixing naive and aware datetimes.

title: the fetched row is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: `session.get(...)` returns None for a deleted delivery and the next line assigns `row.status`, raising AttributeError inside the finalisation path.

title: only httpx.HTTPError is caught
what_is_wrong: any other failure — serialisation TypeError, DetachedInstanceError, DB error from `_finish` — escapes the loop, leaving the row `in_flight` with no terminal status.

title: asyncio.gather without return_exceptions
what_is_wrong: the first delivery to raise propagates out of `gather`, out of the `try`, and terminates the worker's `while True` loop entirely.

title: `batch` can be referenced before assignment
what_is_wrong: if `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` runs and the exception propagates, but on any path where the exception is handled upstream the trailing `if not batch` reads an unbound local.

title: follow_redirects=True on outbound customer requests
what_is_wrong: the client follows 3xx responses, so a registered public URL can redirect the signed payload to an internal host or downgrade it to plaintext http.

title: the HMAC signature is written to the application log
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` logs the full header dict at INFO on every attempt, exposing the signature (and any credentials embedded in the URL) to log storage.

title: the remote response body is stored unbounded
what_is_wrong: `response.text` from an untrusted endpoint is written straight into `response_body`, so a hostile receiver can persist arbitrarily large content per attempt.

title: endpoint.active is not re-checked at send time
what_is_wrong: activity is filtered only when the row is enqueued, so an endpoint deactivated afterwards still receives every already-queued delivery.

title: no bound on concurrent outbound requests
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fires all 100 batch deliveries at once, with no per-host or global concurrency limit.

title: the loop busy-spins whenever the batch is non-empty
what_is_wrong: `await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)` is only reached when `batch` is falsy, so a non-empty batch immediately re-enters the lock/claim cycle with no pause.

title: declared async but performs only blocking work
what_is_wrong: there is no `await` in the body, so the endpoint query and inserts block the event loop while pretending to be awaitable.

title: the returned count is computed before the insert is durable
what_is_wrong: `return len(rows)` runs before the session commits, so callers are told rows were enqueued even when the flush or commit subsequently fails.

title: permanent failure has no side effect beyond the row status
what_is_wrong: reaching `failed_permanent` neither notifies anyone nor deactivates a consistently failing endpoint, so dead endpoints are retried five times per event forever.

title: no cancellation or shutdown handling
what_is_wrong: `while True` has no `asyncio.CancelledError` path, so a shutdown during a batch abandons rows in `in_flight` and leaves the redis lock behind.

title: the signing secret comes from the non-cryptographic random module
what_is_wrong: `random.choice` uses a Mersenne Twister seeded from process state, so observing a few generated secrets allows the remaining ones to be predicted.

title: signature comparison is not constant time
what_is_wrong: `expected == signature` short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking the correct digest through timing while the docs tell customers to use a constant-time comparison.

title: the timestamp is not covered by the MAC
what_is_wrong: the HMAC input is only the serialised payload, so an attacker replaying a captured request can rewrite `X-Acme-Timestamp` freely and the documented five-minute replay window provides no protection.

title: verify ignores the timestamp the caller received
what_is_wrong: it recomputes a fresh timestamp from `time.time()` and discards it, so it cannot enforce any freshness window and accepts an arbitrarily old signature.

title: json.dumps raises on non-JSON-native payload values
what_is_wrong: payloads containing datetimes, Decimals, or UUIDs raise TypeError with no `default=` handler, and that exception is not among the errors `deliver` catches.

title: SECRET_BYTES names a character count, not bytes
what_is_wrong: the constant is used as the length of an alphanumeric string, so the entropy is 32 characters over a 62-symbol alphabet rather than the 32 bytes the name claims.

title: the status values the code writes are not the ones the schema allows
what_is_wrong: `_finish` writes `failed_permanent` and `STATUSES` declares it, while the migration's CHECK constraint allows only `failed`, so every permanent failure raises a constraint violation.

title: model declares timezone-aware columns while the migration creates naive ones
what_is_wrong: `DateTime(timezone=True)` maps to `timestamptz` but the SQL uses bare `TIMESTAMP`, so offsets are dropped on write and reads come back naive.

title: the signing secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: the column holds the raw HMAC key with no encryption or hashing, so any database dump or read-only replica access yields every customer's secret.

title: the STATUSES tuple is declared but never used
what_is_wrong: nothing validates assignments against it, so `status` accepts any string up to 20 characters at the ORM layer.

title: updated_at has a default but no onupdate
what_is_wrong: only `_finish` sets it explicitly, so status changes made anywhere else (such as the `in_flight` transition in `_claim_batch`) leave a stale timestamp.

title: the full event payload is copied per endpoint with no retention bound
what_is_wrong: each delivery row stores its own JSONB copy of the event body, so an org with several endpoints multiplies retention of potentially sensitive payload data indefinitely.

title: event_id is a bare BigInteger with no foreign key
what_is_wrong: nothing ties a delivery to the events table, so deletion of an event leaves orphaned delivery rows and the dedupe key the docs advertise is unenforced on our side.

title: to_dict omits created_at although the API orders by it
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` sorts by `created_at.desc()` but never returns it, so clients cannot tell when an attempt happened or page through results.

title: UNIQUE index on event_id alone breaks multi-endpoint fan-out
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event` inserts one row per active endpoint for the same `event_id`, so any org with two or more endpoints hits a unique violation and gets no deliveries at all.

title: the CHECK constraint omits the status the code writes
what_is_wrong: the allowed set is `('pending','in_flight','delivered','failed')` while `delivery._finish` writes `failed_permanent`.

title: timestamps are created without time zone
what_is_wrong: `created_at`, `next_attempt_at` and `updated_at` are `TIMESTAMP`, so the aware values the code produces are stored with their offset discarded and compared against `now()` in the server's local zone.

title: a new NOT NULL flag column is added that no code reads
what_is_wrong: the ALTER TABLE introduces `webhooks_enabled DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither the dispatcher nor the API consults it, so the flag is dead and the feature is on for everyone.

title: the organizations ALTER shares a transaction with the table creates
what_is_wrong: the ALTER takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on a hot table for the duration of the whole migration transaction, blocking all reads and writes to organizations.

title: no index supports the claim query's ordering
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` filters on status and orders by `next_attempt_at`, but only a single-column index on `status` exists, so the sort is done on the whole pending set.

title: no index supports the deliveries listing query
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` filters on `endpoint_id` and orders by `created_at desc` with neither column indexed, so the listing scans the deliveries table.

title: no uniqueness on (org_id, url)
what_is_wrong: the same URL can be registered repeatedly for one org, causing duplicate POSTs of every event to the same receiver.

title: no rollback path is provided
what_is_wrong: the migration creates two tables and alters a third with no down section, so a failed deploy has to be reversed by hand.

title: the test captures the body and the signature but never checks one against the other
what_is_wrong: it asserts only that the header starts with `sha256=`, so the mismatch between the signed bytes and the transmitted bytes passes unnoticed even though both are captured.

title: the round-trip test is tautological
what_is_wrong: `verify` calls `sign` internally, so the assertion holds for any implementation of `sign` and pins nothing about the on-the-wire format.

title: the retry and worker logic has no tests
what_is_wrong: `deliver`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock`, `_finish` and `run_worker` — where the retries, locking and status transitions live — are never exercised, only the two pure helpers and `send_once`.

title: the new API routes are untested
what_is_wrong: nothing covers `create_webhook_endpoint`, `list_webhook_endpoints` or `list_deliveries`, so the URL validation and the missing org scoping are unexercised.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal
what_is_wrong: `assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5` restates the source line it imports and cannot fail for any behavioural reason.

title: the test pins exact delays and so forbids the documented jitter
what_is_wrong: parametrising `(1,2),(2,4),(3,8),(4,16)` with exact equality means adding the jitter the docs promise turns the test red.

title: the secret test checks shape only
what_is_wrong: prefix and length assertions pass equally for a CSPRNG and for a constant string, so nothing detects the use of `random`.

title: hand-rolled stand-ins replace the ORM models under test
what_is_wrong: using plain classes with class attributes means the detached-instance behaviour, column types, and JSONB round-tripping of the real models are never exercised.

title: no test asserts the statuses the code writes are accepted by the schema
what_is_wrong: nothing inserts a `failed_permanent` row, so the CHECK-constraint mismatch survives a green suite.

title: the test asserts httpx's own behaviour, not the code's
what_is_wrong: `send_once` contains no error handling, so the test only confirms that MockTransport's raised `ConnectError` travels up an `await`.

title: the documented URL restriction is not what the code enforces
what_is_wrong: the validator accepts any scheme beginning with `http`, so plaintext endpoints are registrable despite the stated https-only rule.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "it cannot be read back afterwards"
title: the documented secrecy guarantee is false
what_is_wrong: `GET /v1/settings/webhook-endpoints` returns `signing_secret` for every endpoint.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately"
title: the documented 4xx behaviour contradicts the retry loop
what_is_wrong: `deliver` retries every non-2xx status up to MAX_ATTEMPTS.

title: the documented signing input does not match sign()
what_is_wrong: `sign` HMACs a re-serialised, key-sorted JSON string with no timestamp prefix, so a customer following the docs will never reproduce our signature.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "reject requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old"
title: the documented replay defence cannot work
what_is_wrong: because the timestamp is outside the MAC, an attacker replaying a captured body can set the header to the current time and still pass verification.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "returns the most recent attempts for an endpoint belonging to your organization"
title: the documented ownership scoping is not implemented
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` never filters by `org_id`, so the endpoint returns attempts for any endpoint id.

title: the documented jitter does not exist
what_is_wrong: `backoff_for` returns a fixed `2**attempt` seconds.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "delivery is at-least-once, so deduplicate on event_id"
title: the at-least-once claim is not backed by the code
what_is_wrong: enqueue failures are swallowed in the dispatcher and the unique index on `event_id` rejects fan-out rows, so events can be dropped outright, and `event_id` is not present in the POSTed body to deduplicate on.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "we POST every subscribed event to it"
title: the documented event coverage overstates the wiring
what_is_wrong: only the three types in `WEBHOOK_EVENT_TYPES` reach the webhook path, regardless of what an endpoint subscribes to.

title: the docs omit behaviour the code has
what_is_wrong: nothing documents the 30-second request timeout, the redirect-following, the `in_flight` state visible in the deliveries API, or the per-org `webhooks_enabled` flag the migration introduces.
